decisions.reason: As a large German machinery firm with R&D and public growth ambitions in smarter production, management is likely to keep this established-fit product because it has already invested in it, kept it visible through 2024, and can read any underperformance as temporary in a growing market.

This centrifuge sits squarely within the firm's coolant-management offering, so escalation of commitment, prior engineering investment, and continued website presence make withdrawal within a year unlikely despite room for mixed early results.

Although slightly less core than the products directly building on the established range, this conveyor is still close to the firm's core automation and chip-handling business, so management would tend to justify and continue the launch rather than reverse course quickly.

Because the hinged belt chip conveyor extends the firm's existing material-flow and production-support portfolio and remained marketed in 2024, management would probably persist with it and attribute any disappointment to ramp-up or customer adoption timing rather than drop it now.
